Minnes noticed his absences from the office, hoping this would make him mind his business better. he was more troubled by neglecting to write properly to Mr. Coventry, falling asleep during his letter and making forty blotts and blurrs, and hoped he had not already given offence. the next morning, his monthly accounts agreed within 10s., and he found with great joy that he had gained above L100 clear and was worth above L1400, the greatest sum he had ever possessed. after admiring Mr. Spong’s modesty and ingenuity, he visited Woolwich and Deptford. he ended the month content with his estate and gettings, troubled by his pains and expected rubs over Tangier, and recording great fears of sickness in the City after reports that houses had been shut up.

Amid departures from town, he hoped the Duke had not gone to stay. After a merry dinner with Mrs. Hunt, he worked at the office and on letters until night. Finding the days sensibly shorter without having once shut up the office by daylight, he compared his life to winter and resolved to try for a month what he could do by daylight.
